findings.title: NPE fix applied only to getSubGroupsCount, not to the getSubGroupsStream overloads that have the same pattern
findings.body: The PR fixes the NPE caused by a concurrently deleted group only in getSubGroupsCount() (which now null-checks the result of modelSupplier.get()). However, the three getSubGroupsStream overloads at lines 256, 262 and 268 still call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` without any null check. modelSupplier.get() resolves the group from the database via cacheSession.getGroupDelegate().getGroupById(), which returns null when the group has just been deleted by another thread/request while a stale CachedGroup is still in the cache. Any admin or API call that paginates or searches subgroups of a group that is deleted concurrently (e.g. GET /groups/{id}/children with search/first/max) will still throw a NullPointerException — the exact failure mode this PR claims to fix. These call sites need the same null handling (delegate to empty stream or invalidate) as getSubGroupsCount.

findings.title: Reader thread is never joined, so the assertion races with in-flight requests and can miss exceptions
findings.body: In createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti, the background reader thread is started and never joined. The main thread sets deletedAll to true immediately after the delete loop and then asserts `caughtExceptions` is empty. A GET request that was issued before the flag was set (or that is still in flight) can fail with the very exception this test is supposed to catch and add it to caughtExceptions after the assertThat has already run, so a regression can pass silently. Conversely, the thread can also still be executing when the test method returns, leaking work into the next test against the same realm. The test should capture the thread, set the flag, call thread.join(timeout), and only then assert on caughtExceptions.

findings.title: Test relies on an unbounded, timing-dependent race and never asserts the fixed code path is exercised
findings.body: The test's only synchronization is the hope that the reader thread happens to issue a GET /groups request in the window while groups are being deleted. There is no guarantee that a request lands in the window where a stale CachedGroup for a deleted group is read, so the test can pass even if the NPE regression is reintroduced (it did not deterministically reproduce issue #40368). At minimum the test should assert that the reader thread actually completed some iterations while deletions were in progress (e.g. count successful reads and assert > 0 during the deletion window), otherwise it is a flaky/no-op regression guard.

findings.title: getSubGroupsCount now returns null for a deleted group, a new value in the GroupModel contract
findings.body: When the underlying group no longer exists in the database, GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount() now returns null instead of throwing. GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() implementations (JPA, map, etc.) never return null, so callers may safely unbox the Long or chain comparisons (e.g. `group.getSubGroupsCount() == 0` or `long c = group.getSubGroupsCount()`), which would now produce an NPE at a different, less diagnosable location. In the admin REST path this silently produces a GroupRepresentation with a null/omitted subGroupCount for a group the client believes exists. Returning 0L, or invalidating and surfacing a proper 'group not found', would keep the contract intact.
